Definition: Treating mere possibility as probability — because something could happen, it is treated as if it will. Possibility alone sets no odds.
Example: Someone argues, 'This bridge could collapse, so we must never cross it.'
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone argues, 'Someone could be offended, so we must never preach.'
HowToRespond: Ask the odds: "Possibility isn't probability — how likely is it, really?"
